doc: SurfaceTerms of surface_terms: the six maps (anomaly, land, deck, orographic, continentality, deck_strength: the SurfaceTerms dataclass fields in order) and the ITCZ shift. The smooth terms are computed at tw = min(term_width, width) and resampled to `width` when tw != width; anomaly = land + deck + orographic with land = land_contrast(x) (EARTH_cont(x) - cont), deck = 0.35 (deck_window(x) strength - EARTH_deck(x)). Inputs surface_land and (only when a wind is given) surface_elevation_km: the elevation is read only through the wind; the maps keep the SurfaceTerms field names. The Earth centering tables EARTH_TABLE_X / EARTH_CONTINENTALITY / EARTH_DECK (module constants of surface.py, read by earth_tables_at) are the inputs earth_table_x, earth_table_continentality and earth_table_deck. The coast threshold of deck_strength is at least 1e-4 from every continentality texel (asserted), so no rounding of a port flips it. Tolerance: atol 2e-6, rtol 1e-5: measured worst difference against an all-float64 evaluation 7.4e-8, and 1.2e-7 when land, elevation and wind move by one float32 ulp (10x). Default itcz_shift_deg tolerance 1e-9. width 64 with term_width 1024: tw = 64 = width, the 128x64 surface is box-averaged to 64x32 by `at`, no final resampling; a 2500 km body, Hadley 90 (x below 1: the Earth tables stay near their first nodes and the deck window stays small), prograde, no wind. Output `itcz_shift_deg` is 0-d: shape [] in case.json, one item of data.bin. params.constants lists the module constants and the inline numbers the function reads (a port copies them from its own source and may assert that they equal these).
